subject: baffling problem with mean cluster size calculations in Distance

messages.author: 56a885178ca0e59a
messages.subject: baffling problem with mean cluster size calculations in Distance
parts:
well, at least it remains baffling to me after a couple days trying to
resolve it (and searching the discussion board archives).

Context:
- aerial surveys of moose, line transect sampling, stratified design.
- due to limited encounter rate in each strata, want to use global
estimate of cluster size.
- in order to match past analyses, estimate cluster size as average across
just those clusters detected within 200m of transect.

Bafflement:
Cluster Size / Global Estimates
Effort : 1765.563
# samples : 132
Width : 155.0000 #NOTE: 200-blind strip width
# observations: 43
Expected cluster size estimated as average of cluster size measurements.
Mean cluster size = 0.72093 Standard error = 0.20194

(i) all clusters of moose contain at least 1 moose, so mean cluster size
should be > 1
(and the 'Cluster Size' values of the observation layer are all > = 1);
(ii) data layers appear to have been imported correctly, including
'Cluster Size' field;
(iii) doing this calculation in R, the 43 observations give:
a mean size of 1.7209 (= Distance estimate +1, but perhaps I'm
being paranoid),
SE 0.1318 (!= 0.20194).


Clearly something is wrong somewhere, presumably in what I'm asking
DISTANCE to do.
ANY SUGGESTIONS?

some other relevant summaries to demonstrate I've checked the obvious (to
me) possible sources:

(from Estimation Options)
Parameter Estimation Specification
----------------------------------
Encounter rate by stratum
Detection probability for all data combined
Expected cluster size for all data combined
Density by stratum
Pooled estimate of density is made from area weighted stratum estimates

...
Clusters:
---------
Analysis based on exact sizes
Include s(i) only if x(i) <= 155.0000
Expected value of cluster size computed by: simple average
...

####
I'm happy to consolidate any replies for a summary post to the list.

Cheers,
Joel
